newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia upgrade depends on fiscal tightening-S&P.
newsitem.headline: Australia upgrade depends on fiscal tightening-S&P.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Wednesday that an upgrade of Australia's debt rating depended on the government delivering on its budget tightening and debt reduction plans.
"An upgrade of the Commonwealth's foreign currency rating over the medium term is contingent on the Comonwealth delivering on its fiscal tightening and debt reduction program," S&P said.

"Another key factor in any further upward movement in the rating would be a reduction in Australia's net public external debt position to be more in line with those of similarly rated sovereigns," S&P said.
S&P said the surplus estimates of 0.2 percent and 0.9 percent of GDP in fiscal 1999 and 2000 respectively are expected to be realised as a result of this year's budget.

Although the underlying budget balance did not turn from deficit to surplus until fiscal 1999 the government would be paying down significant amounts of debt from fiscal 1998 and throughout the forward estimates period, it said.

This is a result of a large asset sale programme which is estimated to realise A$9.8 billion in 1997/98. Commonwealth general government net debt is estimated to fall to 10.5 percent of GDP at June 2001 from 19 percent at June 1996, it said.

S&P said the foreign currency and local currency ratings balance Australia's diverse and increasingly competitive economy and narrowing fiscal imbalances with a high net public external debt burden relative to similarly rated sovereigns.

The local currency rating of AAA on long term debt reflected a stronger capapcity to service Australian debt than foreign currency debt as a result of moderate inflation, manageable public finances, and the Commonwealth's taxation powers and control of the domestic financial system, the agency said.
